hero.headline: Judge orders Trump to respond to fraud allegations in IRS settlement case
hero.body:
A federal judge has ordered President Trump to address allegations of fraud related to a settlement with the IRS that ended years of audits. The judge reopened a lawsuit in which Trump is demanding $10 billion from the IRS.

The court order requires Trump to respond to claims that the settlement, which created his $1.8 billion payout fund, involved fraudulent practices. The fund has drawn scrutiny from lawmakers and legal experts since its announcement.

The settlement in question resolved long-running IRS audits of Trump's tax returns. Under the terms of the agreement, Trump established what he calls an anti-weaponization fund, though the specific details of how the settlement led to this fund creation have not been publicly disclosed.

The judge's decision to reopen the case comes as Republican lawmakers are seeking ways to limit or eliminate the $1.8 billion fund. A separate federal judge has already temporarily blocked Trump from immediately setting up the fund, creating a legal tangle around the money.

The fraud allegations center on whether the settlement agreement itself was obtained through improper means. The nature of the specific fraud claims has not been detailed in public court filings, but the judge characterized them as serious enough to warrant a response from the president.

Trump's legal team will now need to file a formal response addressing whether the settlement involved any fraudulent conduct. The timeline for that response has not been publicly announced.

The IRS lawsuit is separate from the ongoing political battle over the fund itself. Some Trump allies have urged him to abandon the fund entirely rather than continue fighting legal and legislative challenges. Senate Republicans face what sources describe as a politically difficult position on the issue, caught between supporting the president and addressing concerns about the fund's legitimacy and size.

The case adds another legal matter to Trump's plate as he continues to serve as president while defending multiple lawsuits related to his personal finances and business dealings.

cards.headline: Iran Launches Missiles at Kuwait Base, Injuring Americans
cards.body:
Iran fired missiles that struck a base in Kuwait, injuring American personnel and damaging US drones, according to US Central Command. The attack represents what the US described as a violation of a fragile ceasefire.

The missile debris caused injuries to Americans stationed at the Kuwait base. US officials characterized the strike as an egregious breach of the truce agreement between the two nations.

The attack comes as President Trump deliberates over a proposed agreement with Iran to pause hostilities. Trump met with advisers to make what he called a final determination on whether to proceed with a framework deal that US and Iranian officials had reportedly agreed upon.

The strike occurred against a backdrop of mixed signals from the White House about the Iran deal. Trump has wavered publicly on whether to move forward with an agreement aimed at ending the war. He vowed to announce his decision soon.

The proposed framework would establish a two-month pause in the conflict, according to reports. However, Iran's missile launch appears to have complicated the diplomatic efforts. US officials confirmed that the attack tested the already fragile truce between Washington and Tehran.

No deal was announced following Trump's meeting with advisers. The president had previously indicated he would make a final decision after consulting with his national security team.

The Middle East remains on edge as regional powers await Trump's determination. The missile strike in Kuwait has raised questions about Iran's commitment to the negotiated framework and whether the ceasefire can hold.

US Central Command released a statement addressing what it termed recent Iranian aggression. The command provided details about the missile debris impact at the Kuwait facility and the resulting damage to military equipment.

The incident marks a significant escalation at a critical moment in US-Iran relations. The attack on American personnel and assets comes just as diplomatic channels appeared to be making progress toward reducing tensions in the region.

cards.headline: Ebola Outbreak Surges in Remote Mining Town
cards.teaser: A gold mining town faces rising deaths and infections as medical workers struggle to contain the virus.
cards.body:
The World Health Organization has confirmed a death rate of 30-50% for the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, meaning up to five of every ten infected people are likely to die. The WHO chief arrived in Kinshasa to support containment efforts.

The outbreak has been complicated by armed group activity in the region. The WHO is calling for a ceasefire among armed groups to prevent deaths from the preventable disease and allow medical teams to work effectively.

cards.headline: Former CDC director warns Ebola outbreak could become second largest in history
cards.teaser: Robert Redfield said the current outbreak has already become the third-largest spread of Ebola in the world.
cards.body:
Robert Redfield, former director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, warned that the current Ebola outbreak could become the second-largest in history. He noted that the outbreak has already reached third-largest status on record.

The World Health Organization's chief traveled to Congo's capital, Kinshasa, to assess response efforts against the outbreak of this rare Ebola virus strain. The situation has prompted concerns among public health officials about potential escalation.

cards.headline: US Defense Secretary Tells Asian Allies to Increase Military Spending
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Hegseth said the US expects Asian partners to boost their own defense capabilities.
cards.body:
At Singapore's Shangri-La Dialogue security summit, Defense Secretary Hegseth reassured Asian allies of continued US commitment while calling for greater defense spending. He emphasized that the United States is not withdrawing its support, though he fielded questions about future arms deals and the depth of American engagement in the region.

Hegseth urged Asian leaders to strengthen their military capabilities in response to China's military expansion, which he described as a "rightful alarm." He notably took a more measured tone on US-China relations and avoided discussing Taiwan during his remarks, while contrasting his praise for Asian partners with criticism aimed at European nations.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth urges Asian allies to increase military spending
cards.teaser: Hegseth told Asian leaders there is rightful alarm about China's military buildup but struck a moderate tone on broader US-China relations.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth called on Asian leaders to increase military spending amid China's expanding military capabilities. Speaking at a security summit in Singapore, Hegseth emphasized there is "rightful alarm" about China's military buildup and stressed the importance of regional defense investments.

While warning about Chinese military expansion, Hegseth took a more measured approach to U.S.-China relations overall. He notably avoided mentioning Taiwan during his remarks, a significant departure from typical defense discussions in the region. The defense secretary also addressed concerns about U.S. commitment to Asian allies, including questions about future arms deals.

cards.headline: DNA test could help breast cancer patients avoid chemotherapy, study finds
cards.teaser: An international trial found that millions of breast cancer patients could safely skip chemotherapy based on a new screening test.
cards.body:
A groundbreaking genomic test could allow millions of breast cancer patients to forgo chemotherapy, according to findings from an international trial. The test identifies patients with low risk scores who can be safely treated with hormone therapy alone, achieving near-identical health outcomes.

Currently, chemotherapy is routinely recommended after surgery when doctors assess there's a risk of disease recurrence. This new DNA screening tool could transform treatment guidelines worldwide by sparing many patients from the side effects of chemotherapy while maintaining their survival prospects.

cards.headline: Drone Crash Into Romanian Apartment Building Brings War Close to Home
cards.teaser: A drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania, highlighting the proximity of the Russia-Ukraine war.
cards.body:
A Russian drone hit an apartment building in eastern Romania, triggering an explosion and fire. NATO and the EU condemned Russia for the incident. Romanian officials believe their air defences struck the drone over Ukrainian territory, causing it to change course before hitting the residential block.

The crash underscored the dangers faced by those living near the conflict zone. Residents experienced panic as the impact damaged their homes, serving as a stark reminder that the Russia-Ukraine war affects communities beyond the battlefield.

cards.headline: Five Rescued From Laos Cave After More Than a Week
cards.teaser: Rescuers freed five people who had been trapped in a flooded cave in Laos for over a week.
cards.body:
Five people have been rescued from a flooded cave in Laos after more than a week trapped underground. The seven villagers entered the narrow cave tunnels on May 20 while searching for gold. One man was freed on Friday, followed by four more men rescued by divers navigating through muddy water and sharp rocks. The rescued individuals were able to walk out of the cave rather than requiring the underwater rescue techniques teams had prepared.

Two villagers remain missing as rescue efforts continue. Divers are working through the hazardous conditions created by water flooding and rock collapses within the cave system.

cards.headline: Japan Immigration Crackdown Forces Foreign Business Owners to Leave
cards.teaser: New visa rules under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi are affecting foreign business owners who have established themselves in Japan.
cards.body:
Japan has implemented new visa rules that are compelling some foreign business owners to leave the country. The changes have particularly affected curry shop operators who have built businesses and put down roots in Japan.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's administration introduced the stricter immigration policies. The crackdown has caught foreign entrepreneurs in its scope, forcing departures among those who had established long-term operations in the country.

cards.headline: US, UK and Australia Develop Underwater Drone Technology
cards.teaser: The three nations are creating new underwater drone capabilities under the Aukus military pact.
cards.body:
The United States, United Kingdom and Australia are collaborating on underwater drone technology through their Aukus military partnership. The systems are designed to protect undersea cables and strengthen naval defence capabilities across the three nations.

This initiative expands the scope of cooperation under the Aukus pact, which brings together the three countries to address shared security interests in the Indo-Pacific region.

cards.headline: Federal judge blocks Trump's $1.8 billion payout fund as GOP lawmakers seek limits
cards.teaser: A federal judge has temporarily barred the president from setting up the fund while Republican lawmakers explore legislative options to restrict it.
cards.body:
A federal judge has temporarily blocked President Trump from establishing his $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund. The legal order creates an additional obstacle for the initiative, which is already facing resistance from Republican lawmakers.

Senate Republicans are considering legislative options to restrict or eliminate the fund entirely. Some Trump allies have privately suggested he drop the effort rather than continue pursuing it, according to reports. The political situation has proven challenging for GOP members navigating their response to the fund.

cards.headline: White House releases Trump health exam results
cards.teaser: The president's physician says Trump is in excellent health and fully fit to serve, though recommends weight loss and more exercise.
cards.body:
President Trump's physician released a memo confirming the president remains in excellent health with strong cardiac, pulmonary, neurological and overall physical function. The examination noted some minor issues including lower leg swelling and benign hand bruising.

The memo was released by the White House following Trump's recent medical evaluation. This marks the fourth hospital visit during his second term.

cards.headline: No Iran deal announced after Trump holds meeting with advisers
cards.teaser: The president met with advisers to make a final determination on a potential agreement after officials confirmed a framework had been reached.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his advisers to make a final determination on a potential Iran deal. No agreement was announced following the meeting.

The US and Iran had previously agreed on a framework for a deal, marking progress in negotiations between the two countries. However, Trump's meeting with advisers did not result in a formal announcement of a completed agreement.

cards.headline: US, UK and Australia to develop underwater drone technology
cards.teaser: The three countries will develop drones under the Aukus military pact to protect undersea cables and enhance naval defense.
cards.body:
The United States, United Kingdom and Australia are developing underwater drone technology through their Aukus military partnership. The initiative aims to protect undersea cables and strengthen naval defense capabilities.

This project expands the scope of Aukus beyond its original focus on nuclear submarine cooperation, demonstrating the alliance's broader commitment to advanced defense technologies in the Indo-Pacific region.

hero.headline: SpaceX plans $80 billion IPO with most shares already allocated
hero.body:
SpaceX is preparing for an initial public offering valued at $80 billion, but 78% of the shares have already been allocated before the public offering begins. The company founded by Elon Musk has structured the IPO in a way that limits availability to general investors.

Wall Street banks working on the offering face competing pressures. Investment firms want access to what could be one of the largest technology IPOs in recent years, but they also worry about the risks of the company underperforming after going public. Musk and his bankers are trying to generate enough demand that investors feel missing the offering poses a greater risk than participating in it.

The IPO has already affected other space-related stocks. Rocket Lab and AST SpaceMobile have experienced trading volatility that some analysts compare to patterns seen in electric vehicle stocks during previous market bubbles. Short sellers betting against these companies have faced significant losses as stock prices surged.

SpaceX generates most of its revenue from a business segment that may surprise investors expecting the company to focus primarily on space exploration and launches. The company has diversified its operations beyond rocket launches, though the specific revenue source was not detailed in available information.

The structure of the offering has drawn attention from market observers who note that pre-allocated shares reduce the opportunity for typical retail and institutional investors to participate at the initial offering price. This approach differs from traditional IPOs where a larger percentage of shares become available to the broader market at launch.

The $80 billion valuation would place SpaceX among the most valuable private companies to go public in recent years. The offering comes as investor appetite for technology stocks remains strong, particularly in sectors related to artificial intelligence and advanced manufacturing. How the market responds to the IPO could influence other private technology companies considering whether to pursue public offerings in the coming months.

cards.headline: Dell stock hits record high on strong AI-driven data center demand
cards.teaser: Dell Technologies shares surged to an all-time high after the company raised its financial forecasts, driven by demand from artificial intelligence data center construction.

cards.headline: United Airlines flight diverted after passenger attempts cockpit breach
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison, Wisconsin after a passenger tried to breach the cockpit during the flight.
cards.body:
The airline diverted the flight and detained an unruly passenger following the security incident. Audio recordings indicate the diversion was prompted by an attempted cockpit breach, according to reports from Wisconsin news outlets.

The aircraft landed safely in Madison where law enforcement met the plane and took the passenger into custody. United Airlines confirmed the flight was diverted due to a security concern involving a disruptive passenger. The remaining passengers continued to their destination after the incident was resolved.

cards.headline: China expands use of digital yuan to government spending and lotteries
cards.teaser: China has broadened the applications of its digital currency to include lottery draws and fiscal spending by government agencies.
cards.body:
The Chinese government is broadening the use of its central bank digital currency beyond initial pilot programs. The digital yuan is now being used for government fiscal transactions and lottery systems, according to Reuters reporting.

This expansion reflects China's efforts to establish the digital yuan more widely across the economy. The development is being monitored closely by other countries as they track China's central bank digital currency progress.

cards.headline: Replimune plans third FDA submission for cancer drug after agency talks
cards.teaser: Replimune will resubmit its melanoma treatment for FDA approval after the agency rejected the application twice previously.
cards.body:
The biotechnology company said it will ask the FDA to review its cancer drug again following what it described as productive discussions with the agency. The drug had been rejected in two previous submission attempts.

Replimune stock jumped 80% on the announcement. The resubmission follows changes at the FDA and what the company characterized as constructive dialogue with regulators. The agency has stood by its past rejections but appears willing to reconsider the application with additional information.

cards.headline: New York passes tax on luxury second homes
cards.teaser: New York lawmakers approved a tax on expensive properties used as secondary residences, with questions remaining about implementation.
cards.body:
The state legislature passed the pied-a-terre tax targeting high-value properties owned by people who do not live in them as primary residences. Citadel founder Ken Griffin, who owns expensive New York real estate, will be among those affected by the new levy.

Implementing the tax presents challenges for lawmakers and property managers, particularly for cooperative apartment buildings. New York City property tax assessments are expected to rise as real estate values increase. The tax aims to generate revenue from owners of luxury second homes in the city.

cards.headline: China's biotechnology advances challenge US pharmaceutical dominance
cards.teaser: Chinese clinical trials are drawing attention at an international cancer conference as the country's biotechnology sector grows rapidly.
cards.body:
Clinical trials conducted in China are attracting significant attention at an international oncology conference in Chicago. The country's biotechnology industry has experienced rapid expansion, prompting concerns among US researchers and policymakers about America's competitive position in pharmaceutical development.

China's growing drug development capabilities represent a notable shift in the global pharmaceutical landscape. The surge in Chinese clinical research has fueled alarm that US dominance in biotechnology may be declining.

hero.headline: Nvidia to debut first Windows PCs with its own chips
hero.body:
Nvidia will introduce the first Windows computers powered by its own processors next week, according to reports. The debut represents a significant shift for the graphics chip maker into the PC processor market.

The computers will run on Nvidia's new N1X laptop processors. Microsoft and Arm have joined Nvidia in promoting the upcoming launch through social media posts ahead of an event. The processors mark Nvidia's entry into direct competition with established PC chip makers.

The announcement comes as Nvidia expands beyond its traditional graphics processing unit business. The company has posted what it describes as cryptic messages on social media platforms in the days leading up to its GTC event, where the new processors are expected to be formally revealed.

The move puts Nvidia in the Windows PC processor space alongside existing players. Arm is also involved in the chip architecture, suggesting the processors will use Arm-based designs rather than the x86 architecture that has dominated Windows PCs for decades.

Microsoft's participation in the promotional campaign indicates support for the new platform. The software giant has previously worked to expand Windows compatibility with Arm-based processors, though adoption has remained limited compared to traditional PC chips.

The N1X processors represent Nvidia's attempt to leverage its chip design expertise in a new market segment. The company has seen substantial growth in recent years driven by demand for its graphics processors in artificial intelligence applications and gaming.

The timing of the launch coincides with broader industry interest in alternative processor architectures for personal computers. Several manufacturers have experimented with Arm-based designs as potential alternatives to traditional PC chips.

Nvidia has not disclosed technical specifications for the N1X processors or which computer manufacturers will offer devices using the chips. The full details are expected to be announced at next week's event.

cards.headline: Sea cucumber tissue survives years after amputation
cards.teaser: Scientists are studying chunks of sea cucumber tissue that have continued living for several years after being severed from the body.
cards.body:
Researchers have observed amputated sea cucumber parts showing what they describe as signs of immortality. The severed tissue continues to heal itself and survive for years after being detached from the animal's body.

The appendages do not appear to die even after extended periods of separation. Scientists believe the findings could have implications for medical research, though they have not specified what applications might emerge from studying the tissue's survival mechanisms.

cards.headline: Venture capitalists discuss AI startup investment surge
cards.teaser: Three prominent venture capital investors describe an intense competition for young AI entrepreneurs in San Francisco.
cards.body:
Venture capitalists are offering seed funding term sheets to 22-year-old AI founders in San Francisco, with even younger entrepreneurs receiving Series A offers. One investor said, half-jokingly, that 19-year-old founders building in AI might already have Series A funding offers because their youth signals exceptional ability.

The comments reflect what investors characterize as groupthink in the current AI investment environment. The remarks came during a discussion about the state of AI funding and the pace at which capital is being deployed to young founders working on artificial intelligence projects.

cards.headline: TikTok expands beyond social media platform
cards.teaser: TikTok may be developing into a super app where users handle most of their digital activities.
cards.body:
The social media company appears to be working toward becoming a comprehensive platform for digital tasks beyond video sharing. The effort would transform TikTok from a specialized social network into an application that handles a broader range of user needs.

The expansion reflects a strategy seen in other markets where single apps provide multiple services including messaging, payments, and shopping. TikTok has not publicly detailed which specific features or services it plans to add as part of this evolution.

cards.headline: Volcanic eruption may offer method to reduce greenhouse gas
cards.teaser: A volcanic eruption has potentially revealed a new approach to addressing a potent planet-heating gas.
cards.body:
Scientists studying a violent volcanic eruption say the event may have uncovered a weapon against a greenhouse gas. The research suggests volcanic processes could provide insights into methods for tackling atmospheric pollutants.

The discovery emerged from analysis of the eruption's effects on atmospheric chemistry. Researchers have not specified which greenhouse gas the method might address or provided details on how the volcanic activity could be applied to climate solutions.

cards.headline: New book examines history of vaccine opposition
cards.teaser: A recently published book traces the long history of vaccine opponents across different eras and motivations.
cards.body:
The book categorizes vaccine opposition figures into three groups: grifters, cynics, and true believers. The author examines how these different types of opponents have shaped public health debates over time.

The work provides historical context for understanding modern vaccine resistance. It explores the motivations and tactics of those who have fought against vaccination campaigns across multiple generations and in various forms.

cards.headline: Trump administration proposes coal ash monitoring changes
cards.teaser: The administration wants to shift coal ash oversight to states and allow bypassing of national standards.
cards.body:
Environmental groups are opposing the Trump administration's proposed changes to coal ash regulations. The plan would shift monitoring and enforcement responsibilities from federal agencies to state governments, allowing states to bypass national standards for coal ash management.

Environmentalists have mobilized to contest the rollbacks, arguing they would weaken protections against coal ash contamination.

hero.headline: Liverpool parts ways with manager Arne Slot after two seasons
hero.body:
Liverpool fired head coach Arne Slot after two seasons in charge, the club announced. Slot won the Premier League title with Liverpool during his tenure but was dismissed as the club seeks a change in direction.

The departure marks a sharp reversal of fortune for Slot, who delivered a league championship just a year ago. Liverpool released an official statement confirming the decision but provided no additional details about the reasons behind the move.

Chief football writer Phil McNulty described Slot's dismissal as one of the most remarkable falls from grace in Premier League history. The speed of the decline from title winner to fired manager has drawn widespread attention across English football.

Andoni Iraola has emerged as the leading candidate to replace Slot as Liverpool's next head coach. The club has not confirmed any appointment or formally commented on potential successors.

Slot's exit comes despite the significant success of winning the Premier League, typically considered the ultimate achievement for any English club manager. The decision suggests Liverpool's leadership identified concerns about the team's direction that outweighed the recent championship.

The club now faces the task of installing a new manager and potentially reshaping the squad. Liverpool has not indicated a timeline for naming Slot's replacement or outlined its vision for the team's future under new leadership.

The firing ends what began as a successful stint for Slot at one of England's most storied clubs. His departure leaves questions about what led Liverpool to part ways with a manager who delivered the sport's most coveted domestic prize so recently.

cards.headline: Song Yadong submits Deiveson Figueiredo in second round at UFC Macau
cards.teaser: Song Yadong defeated Deiveson Figueiredo with a guillotine choke in the second round of their main event fight at UFC Macau.
cards.body:
Song Yadong finished Deiveson Figueiredo with a guillotine choke submission in the second round of their headlining bout at UFC Macau. The finish came as a surprise conclusion to the main event.

The submission victory marks a significant win for Song in the bantamweight division. Figueiredo, a former flyweight champion, was unable to escape the choke and was forced to tap out.

cards.headline: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and Abdul Carter address dispute after Trump rally appearance
cards.teaser: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and teammate Abdul Carter addressed their disagreement following Dart's introduction of President Trump at a political rally.
cards.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and defensive player Abdul Carter publicly discussed their recent discord after Dart introduced President Trump at a rally. The two players expressed unity following the disagreement.

Giants quarterbacks coach Jameis Winston said the team has grown from the situation. Coach John Harbaugh appeared unlikely to criticize Dart's political appearance during a Friday press conference.

cards.headline: Scotland coach Steve Clarke worried about Billy Gilmour injury
cards.teaser: Scotland head coach Steve Clarke expressed concern after midfielder Billy Gilmour left the field during a 4-1 friendly victory over Curacao.
cards.body:
Steve Clarke said he is completely worried about Billy Gilmour after the midfielder was substituted during Scotland's 4-1 friendly win against Curacao. The extent of Gilmour's injury has not been disclosed.

Scotland secured the comfortable victory despite losing Gilmour during the match. The midfielder's availability for upcoming fixtures remains uncertain as the team awaits further assessment.

cards.headline: Saracens defeat Harlequins to boost playoff chances
cards.teaser: Saracens beat Harlequins in a match that strengthened their position for the Premiership playoffs and served as a winning farewell for departing director of rugby Mark McCall.
cards.body: Saracens defeated Harlequins at the StoneX Stadium to strengthen their Premiership playoff hopes. The victory provided a winning farewell for departing director of rugby Mark McCall, whose tenure with the club concluded with the home triumph.

cards.headline: Bulls eliminate Munster from United Rugby Championship with six-try victory
cards.teaser: The Bulls scored six tries to defeat Munster in their United Rugby Championship quarter-final in Pretoria, ending the Irish province's title hopes.
cards.body:
The Bulls ended Munster's United Rugby Championship title hopes with a dominant display in their quarter-final clash in Pretoria. The South African side's ruthless attacking performance yielded six tries as they overpowered the Irish province.

The victory secured the Bulls' passage to the semi-finals of the competition, with their comprehensive win demonstrating their strength in the knockout stages.

cards.headline: Wigan retains Women's Challenge Cup with 54-6 victory over St Helens
cards.teaser: Wigan Warriors successfully defended their Women's Challenge Cup title with a commanding 54-6 win over St Helens at Wembley.
cards.body:
Wigan Warriors retained the Women's Challenge Cup with a commanding 54-6 victory over St Helens at Wembley. Eva Hunter was the standout performer, scoring four tries in the dominant display.

The Warriors' clinical execution throughout the match secured back-to-back titles for the club. Their superiority was evident from start to finish against their rivals.

hero.headline: A24 Sets Box Office Record With 'Backrooms' Opening
hero.body:
Independent studio A24 set a new company record with the opening weekend of "Backrooms," which earned between $85 million and $89 million at the box office. The film marks the highest opening in A24's history, surpassing all previous releases from the studio known for prestige and indie fare.

The success represents part of a larger trend of movies adapted from YouTube content finding mainstream theatrical success. "Backrooms" joins other recent films from digital creators in proving that online audiences can translate to box office performance.

Meanwhile, "Obsession" overtook "The Mandalorian and Grogu" at the box office after the Star Wars film's initial run. The shift comes as Disney's Star Wars theatrical releases face questions about the franchise's current direction and audience appeal.

The strong performance of "Obsession" also highlights the business strategy of producers who have built their operations around working with first-time directors. The approach has yielded significant financial returns, with this weekend's results validating the model of investing in new filmmaking talent rather than established names alone.

A24 has built its reputation on lower-budget films that often become cultural phenomena despite modest marketing campaigns. The studio's previous biggest openings included awards contenders and horror films, but none approached the scale of "Backrooms." The YouTube-to-theater pipeline represents new territory for both A24 and the industry, as studios look for proven intellectual property with built-in audiences.

The weekend's results suggest audiences remain willing to turn out for original content when it connects with their interests, even as franchises like Star Wars face scrutiny. "The Mandalorian and Grogu" had been expected to dominate the box office for multiple weeks based on the popularity of the Disney+ series, making its displacement by "Obsession" a notable shift in the competitive landscape.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Rest of 2026 Tour for Health Reasons
cards.teaser: The Four Seasons singer will take six months off and may resume performing in 2027.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli canceled his remaining 2026 concerts to focus on his health. The Four Seasons singer announced he will take a six-month break from performing.

Valli said he will consider resuming touring in 2027 after the recovery period. The 92-year-old singer had been actively performing before making the decision to step back from the road.

cards.headline: Emily Blunt Declined AI Tools on Spielberg's 'Disclosure Day'
cards.teaser: The actress said she was terrified of artificial intelligence and chose not to use it during a key scene.
cards.body:
Emily Blunt refused to use artificial intelligence during a pivotal sequence in Steven Spielberg's upcoming film "Disclosure Day." The actress said she is terrified of AI technology.

The Spielberg-directed science fiction film stars Blunt as a Kansas City television meteorologist. Her character becomes overcome by a mysterious extraterrestrial force while taping a live weather segment on air.

cards.headline: Ye and Travis Scott Concerts in Italy Canceled Over Security Concerns
cards.teaser: Scheduled performances by the two artists were called off due to security fears.
cards.body:
Concerts by Ye and Travis Scott in Italy were canceled due to security concerns. The New York Times reported the cancellations, though specific details about the nature of the security fears were not provided in available reports.

Both artists had been scheduled to perform in Italy as part of their touring schedules. The cancellations affect fans who had planned to attend the shows.

cards.headline: Vanilla Ice Defends Performance at Trump White House Event
cards.teaser: The rapper said he would perform for any world leader and does not vote.
cards.body:
Vanilla Ice defended his planned performance at the Trump White House Freedom 250 concert after multiple artists dropped out of the event. The rapper said he would perform for Russian President Vladimir Putin or in Iran if asked, emphasizing he keeps his shows non-political.

Vanilla Ice said he does not vote. Several other artists have withdrawn from the Freedom 250 festival scheduled for this summer in Washington, D.C., but the rapper confirmed he will keep his commitment to perform at the event.

cards.headline: Charlie Puth Brings Out Busta Rhymes and Art Garfunkel at Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: The singer featured multiple guest stars during his "Whatever's Clever!" World Tour stop.
cards.body:
Charlie Puth performed at Madison Square Garden as part of his "Whatever's Clever!" World Tour, welcoming special guests including Busta Rhymes, Art Garfunkel, Jimmy Fallon, and Kirk Franklin to the stage.

During the New York show, Puth expressed his gratitude to the audience, saying "This makes it all worth it."

cards.headline: Nicolas Cage Discusses 'Spider-Noir' Season Finale and Potential Return
cards.teaser: The actor spoke about major plot points from the Prime Video series and whether he would return for another season.
cards.body:
Nicolas Cage stars as Ben Reilly, a private investigator in Depression-era New York, in the Prime Video series "Spider-Noir." The show combines film noir aesthetics with superhero storytelling and is shot in black and white, though a color version is also available.

Cage recently discussed the season finale, covering key plot points including character deaths, action sequences, and the spider's sacrifice. He also addressed his potential involvement in a second season should the show be renewed.

hero.headline: Defense Secretary disputes claim Iran war delayed Taiwan arms sale
hero.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth rejected assertions from a military official that ongoing conflict with Iran has caused delays to a $14 billion weapons package intended for Taiwan.

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao told senators the United States was postponing the deal to protect its depleting munitions supplies. The military has been consuming weapons stockpiles at a rapid rate while conducting sustained operations against Iran.

The proposed arms sale to Taiwan would represent one of the largest weapons transfers to the island in recent years. Taiwan has pressed Washington for expanded military assistance as tensions have grown across the region.

Hegseth's contradictory position and Cao's statement expose disagreements within the administration about juggling competing security priorities. The Pentagon faces the difficult task of sustaining weapons supplies for current military campaigns while maintaining its obligations to Pacific allies.

Though the United States does not have formal diplomatic ties with Taiwan, federal law requires it to supply the island with weapons for defensive purposes. Beijing has repeatedly condemned these sales, asserting that Taiwan belongs under its control.

The arms package delay comes as the military confronts inventory shortages across multiple regions. Weapons expenditures from Iran operations have strained supplies that would typically be allocated for foreign military purchases.

The $14 billion package includes air defense systems and anti-ship missiles designed to strengthen Taiwan's defensive capabilities against potential Chinese invasion. Taiwan has sought to modernize its military as China has expanded military exercises surrounding the island.

The disagreement between Hegseth and Cao illustrates the complex position facing the Defense Department as it balances supporting allies with managing active warfare. Weapons manufacturers have struggled to boost production at the pace required to meet competing regional demands.

The timing of this dispute coincides with broader economic pressures stemming from the Iran conflict. Energy costs across allied nations have risen sharply, with households in some countries facing significantly higher utility bills. In the United States, inflation reached its fastest pace in three years in April, driven largely by energy prices related to the war. Economists expect the Federal Reserve to maintain unchanged interest rates through much of the year.

Consumer spending power has declined as prices continue climbing. Surveys show declining public confidence in the administration's economic stewardship, with approval ratings falling even among core supporters. Trump's 2024 election victory relied heavily on pledges to reduce inflation, making economic conditions an increasingly sensitive political issue.

The military supply challenges revealed by the Taiwan arms sale dispute reflect these broader economic consequences of sustained Middle East operations. As the conflict continues, managing weapons production alongside inflation and household financial strain presents mounting political and strategic complications for the administration.

cards.headline: Former CDC director warns Ebola outbreak could become second largest in history
cards.teaser: Robert Redfield said the current outbreak has already become the third-largest spread of Ebola in the world.
cards.body:
Robert Redfield, former director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, warned that the current Ebola outbreak could become the second-largest in history. He noted that the outbreak has already reached third-largest status on record.

The World Health Organization's chief traveled to Congo's capital, Kinshasa, to assess response efforts against the outbreak of this rare Ebola virus strain. The situation has prompted concerns among public health officials about potential escalation.

cards.headline: Trump attacks judge over Kennedy Center name and closure ruling
cards.teaser: President Trump said a federal judge should be ashamed for blocking his administration's move to add his name to the performing arts center.
cards.body:
President Trump criticized U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper after the judge blocked the administration's plan to add Trump's name to the Kennedy Center. In a 94-page ruling, Cooper determined that the arts complex was permanently named for the late President John F. Kennedy and cannot be renamed.

The judge also ruled that the Kennedy Center cannot proceed with a planned two-year closure for renovations, at least for now. Trump responded with a statement saying the judge should be "ashamed of himself" for the decision.

cards.headline: Trump's approval rating hits record low of 34 percent
cards.teaser: Comedian Bill Maher highlighted the president's dismal poll numbers and controversy over a planned National Mall celebration.
cards.body:
President Trump's job approval rating fell to a record low of 34 percent this week, according to a poll conducted by YouGov and The Economist. The drop comes amid blowback to a planned celebration on the National Mall for America's 250th birthday.

Comedian Bill Maher discussed the poll numbers and the controversy surrounding the upcoming bash. The National Mall event has drawn criticism from various quarters.

cards.headline: Credit card delinquencies reach highest rate since 2011
cards.teaser: More than 13 percent of credit card balances were at least 90 days past due in the first quarter.
cards.body:
The share of credit card balances that were at least 90 days past due reached more than 13 percent in the first quarter. This marks the highest delinquency rate since 2011.

The increase in late payments signals growing financial stress among American households. The rise in seriously delinquent accounts reflects broader economic pressures on consumers.

cards.headline: Texas Senate race tests durability of Republican anti-woke strategy
cards.teaser: The contest has become a testing ground for whether culture war messaging still resonates amid economic challenges.
cards.body:
Ken Paxton, the Republican Senate nominee in Texas, has made masculinity a central campaign theme, attacking Democratic state Rep. James Talarico as "too low-T for Texas" following his primary runoff victory. The move exemplifies how Republicans are deploying cultural messaging in the race.

The contest has become a testing ground for whether the anti-woke strategy that resonated with voters in 2020 remains effective, particularly as economic concerns take priority in the 2026 midterm environment. Republicans believe they successfully positioned progressive language and identity politics as symbols of elite detachment and are attempting to replicate that approach in this more challenging political climate.

cards.headline: Nvidia to debut first Windows computers using its chips as main processor
cards.teaser: The chipmaker will unveil the systems at industry conferences next week, giving Microsoft a second attempt at AI PCs.
cards.body:
Nvidia is set to unveil its first Windows computers powered by its own chips as the main processor next week. The move marks the company's direct entry into the PC market, expanding beyond its core business of powering AI systems.

Microsoft and Nvidia will jointly present their work at Computex in Taiwan and at Microsoft's developer conference. The collaboration represents a fresh attempt at the AI PC market for Microsoft, following an earlier initiative that underperformed.
